mechanism: Bumetanide causes electrolyte depletion and hypotension while promethazine has anticholinergic and CNS depressant effects, with additive hypotensive and sedative effects; promethazine may mask signs of ototoxicity from bumetanide.
action: Monitor blood pressure, electrolytes, and renal function regularly; assess for dizziness, syncope, and hearing changes; educate patient on fall risk and avoid concurrent CNS depressants.
